checks: Verified original §§2–3, equations (3)–(5) and the contact-mean calculation. Integrating the accepted positive survival comparison from 0 to dc_z/S_z gives dc_z²/((d+1)S_z). A lower-support section follows by decreasing proper thresholds to it, taking the accepted section area limit and dominated hinge limit; reducing effective section mass only enlarges the bound. Upper-support empty sections have zero hinge.
Indices without effective section contribute h_* exactly. Expanding the square and using Σ_I S_zδ_z=C gives the bracket Σ_I c_z²/S_z. The stated sufficient equality case follows term by term.

With all positive cap mass on I, E_πδ=C/S and E_π[Zδ]=(C/S)z̄_c. Covariance is the displayed mean difference. Its kernel orthogonality gives range membership even for singular base covariance, and expanding with ΣΣ⁺v=v gives the exact residual.

The contact mean is its prescribed first moment divided by C+rS>0. Equal cap and section means set v=0. If δ is affine on I, the centered slope is a coordinate linear combination orthogonal to that whole span, hence zero in the weighted law.

dependencies.hypotheses: Each positive fiber is a convex body and the continuous normal is unit. Its proper-cut survival theorem and its proof of the parallel section limit at lower support apply; the effective weight comparison is then elementary.

overlap.comparison: The accepted survival comparison gives the local hinge inequality after integration, but does not state the mixed section-weighted aggregation, singular regression and contact mean implication.
It gives a different regression for continuous source coordinates and cap-normal labels in a whole-line problem, not the c_z/S_z regression on section-weighted base coordinates.

readability: C counts the cap mass on positive-section fibers. It becomes the entire cap mass only under the extra stated hypothesis.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The sharp local hinge estimates aggregate with exact section-weighted variance, and base moments detect only its affine projection.
